From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Realtime inference errors and prolonged tails in p95 latency

Kimberly / Alice —

Triage update from engineering (short version):
- Observed: sudden spike in token-level retries and KV cache eviction rate correlated with a model variant rollout that started at 07:48 PDT. The rollout introduced a different attention kernel that increases memory pressure under our current batching pattern.
- Impact: increased tail latency -> request timeouts -> retries loop -> higher error rate and reduced effective throughput.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (I recommend executing all in parallel):
1) Re-route 25% of traffic to lumenix-realtime-v2-quant (safer memory footprint) — should reduce client impact within ~3–5 minutes.
2) Temporarily disable the new rollout / pin traffic to last stable model version.
3) Increase replica count for the real-time pool by +30% (estimated 20–40 minutes to be effective depending on capacity).
4) Apply emergency KV-cache eviction threshold bump (stateless change, immediate).

Risk/ask: Re-routing will change numerical output slightly for some edge cases; need Alice/Jacob acknowledgement to proceed. If they cannot accept any variance, we'll avoid reroute and prioritize replica scaling + tuning (slower).

Estimated stabilization: 15–45 minutes if reroute+eviction bump accepted; 30–90 minutes if we only scale replicas and tune.

I will start the pin and eviction change now pending confirmation.

Marissa Cole
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

All —

Post-mortem update and customer-facing summary:
- Incident summary: On 2027-03-22 07:48 PDT a model variant rollout caused increased memory pressure in the real-time pool, leading to cache evictions and a retry loop that raised error rate to ~8% and reduced throughput.
- Immediate response: We pinned traffic to the stable model, applied an emergency KV-cache eviction bump, re-routed 25% of traffic to lumenix-realtime-v2-quant, and provisioned additional reserved capacity. Error rates returned to baseline (~0.5%) and p95/p99 latencies normalized by 11:05 PDT on 2027-03-22.
- Customer impact: Partial requests may have experienced altered numerical outputs for the 25% rerouted traffic window (flagged). No data exposure or loss.
- Ongoing actions:
   * Full RCA scheduled for 2027-03-25 10:00 PDT (invite to follow) — Marissa leading.
   * Proposed customer credit: 2 days of API credits; Kimberly will propose formal credit and legal will prepare language.
   * Action item: Improve rollout gating for kernel-level changes and add a pre-deploy canary that exercises memory/batching edge cases.

Thank you to our on-call and ops teams for rapid response. Neha will follow up with Lumenix on the credit proposal and to coordinate the post-incident review logistics.

Kimberly Park
